info.title: Najeh Backend - Session Changelog API (update-4)
info.description:
OpenAPI spec covering every endpoint ADDED or CHANGED across this project's work, cumulative across update-1, update-2, update-3 and update-4. Import into Apidog via Import > OpenAPI/Swagger. Auth: each role has its own Bearer JWT (Admin/Teacher/Student/Parent security schemes below); AnyAuth accepts a JWT from any one of the 4 roles.

=== WHAT IS NEW IN update-4 ===
update-4 is everything done after update-3 shipped. Search this file for the string 'update-4' to find every affected operation. It adds 42 brand-new paths and ships 12 DB migrations (064, 065, 066, 067, 068, 069, 070, 071, 072, 073, 074, 075), each of which must be run on the database by hand before the matching endpoints will work.

1) DATED APPOINTMENT SLOTS (NEW LAYER, migration 066 `teacher_availability_slots`). A second, parallel scheduling layer next to `class_sessions`. `class_sessions` stays exactly as it was: a weekly recurring pattern (`day_of_week` + `start_time`) with no calendar date on it. A slot is ONE appointment on a REAL date, with a `capacity` (1 = private lesson, higher = group). 15 new endpoints: admin GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /admin/availability plus /admin/availability/generate, /book, /schedule-student; teacher GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /teacher/availability plus /generate and /book; student GET /student/availability, GET /student/availability/my-schedule, POST/DELETE /student/availability/book. CLIENT ACTION: a client that only knows about /sessions will not see these appointments - they are not returned by the session endpoints.

2) PACKAGES NOW EXPIRE (migration 065, `courses.duration_months`). A package (`courses.kind` = 'package') can declare how many months a subscription to it lasts (1, 3, 6 or 12). When a package is granted or redeemed and the caller sends neither `end_date` nor `duration_days`, the subscription's `end_date` is now start + `duration_months`. BEFORE update-4 package access was stored with `end_date` NULL and never expired, so a client that showed 'unlimited' for packages must stop doing that.

3) DISCOUNT CODES (NEW, migrations 069, 070 and 073). Admin access is gated on `manage_discounts` - its own permission since migration 073 - rather than on `manage_teachers`. A discount code REDUCES a price; it is NOT a `subscription_code` (which opens access outright and is free). Separate tables so neither flow can hand out the other's thing.

ADMIN: /admin/discount-codes (list/create/update/delete), /admin/discount-codes/show, /admin/discount-codes/check, /admin/discount-codes/redemptions.

TEACHER (migration 070 cycle): a teacher now owns discount codes of their own - /teacher/discount-codes (list/create/update/delete), /teacher/discount-codes/show, /teacher/discount-codes/check, /teacher/discount-codes/redemptions. A teacher's code can only ever reduce the price of a course that teacher teaches. Leaving `course_ids` empty means 'all MY courses', not the whole platform: at redemption time the code is intersected with the owner's course list, so it can never reach another teacher's work even if it was created before the teacher was removed from a course.

STUDENT: a student can now USE a code, not only preview one. There is no payment gateway in this platform, so using a code cannot mean paying with it - POST /student/discount-codes/apply PINS the code to a course, storing a `pending` row that costs the code nothing. GET /student/discount-codes/my-codes lists what they are holding (read `is_still_valid` before showing one as money off), DELETE /student/discount-codes/cancel drops one. The admin grant then honours that claim on its own: POST /admin/subscriptions with no `discount_code` looks the student's pending claims up and promotes the first still-valid one, so the code never has to survive being relayed by hand.

WHERE A COUPON DOES NOT BELONG: redeeming a SUBSCRIPTION code (POST /student/subscriptions/redeem-code) takes no coupon and ignores one if sent. A subscription code opens access outright and is free, so a student holding one has already paid whoever sold it to them and there is nothing left to reduce. A coupon only ever applies before the money changes hands.

WHEN A CODE IS SPENT: only when a grant actually applies it. Checking is a read, and so is a student's claim. `discount_code_redemptions.status` is what separates them - `pending` (student holding it) from `applied` (discount really given). Any client that sums redemption rows as money discounted must filter on `applied`.

VALIDATION CHANGE (same cycle): applying a code with NO course - a subject-wide or teacher-wide grant - is now refused instead of silently recording a 0.00 discount. The old behaviour spent one of the code's uses and, with `once_per_student`, burnt that code for that student permanently, in exchange for nothing.

4) CERTIFICATES CAN BE GRANTED AND REVOKED (no migration - existing tables). New: /admin/student-certificates (list, grant to one or many students, revoke) and /teacher/student-certificates (list own, revoke own).

5) CURRENCY IS USD (migration 067). `payment_transactions.currency` defaulted to 'EGP' because the EasyKash gateway was wired first; no gateway is actually in use. The column default is now 'USD' and existing rows were relabelled. CLIENT ACTION: hardcoded 'ج.م'/'EGP' labels must become '$'/'USD'.

6) PER-COURSE VIDEO DOWNLOAD (migration 068, `courses.allow_video_download`). Mirrors the pre-existing `course_books.allow_download`. Defaults to 0 (watch in-platform only), deliberately - the protective choice must not depend on someone ticking a box.

7) QUESTION IMAGES (migration 064, `questions.question_image`). An optional image on a question itself (a diagram, a photographed problem). This feature had been edited straight onto production without a commit; update-4 brings it into the tracked codebase. Same operation also relaxes validation: question TEXT is no longer required, so an image-only question is legal.

8) TEACHER HOME REWRITTEN. GET /teacher/home (and its alias GET /teacher/content/home) used to fall back to hardcoded demo data - fake KPI numbers, a fixed 7-month chart, 3 invented 'recent activity' rows - whenever the real query came back empty. Every field is now computed live from the DB. CLIENT ACTION: empty states are now real and must be handled.

9) ADMIN DASHBOARD STATISTICS EXPANDED. GET /admin/dashboard/statistics previously returned only the `statistics` counts. It now also returns sales totals (total/today/month/year), per-course sales, yearly charts, and a bilingual recent-activity feed assembled on the fly from the newest rows of the tables that represent real events (there is no audit-log table). Every label ships in both `_ar` and `_en` so no DB enum value ever reaches the screen untranslated.

10) DEVICE LIMIT ON STUDENT ACCOUNTS (migration 071, `user_devices` + `students.max_devices`). One set of credentials shared around a class was the cheapest way to give a paid course away. A student account may now be signed in from a limited number of devices - ONE by default - and the next new device is refused and told to contact support.

EVERY CLIENT THAT LOGS A STUDENT IN MUST BE UPDATED BEFORE ENFORCEMENT IS SWITCHED ON: send a `device_id` that the client generates once and keeps (or the `X-Device-Id` header). A login with none is refused with `error_code: device_id_required`, and a fresh id per login burns through the student's slots. See POST /user/student/auth/login for the full contract, including the new `device_limit_reached` and `device_revoked` error codes.

ADMIN: GET /admin/students/devices, POST /admin/students/devices/reset (frees the slots so a new device can sign in), POST /admin/students/logout-all (migration 072 - ends every session everywhere while KEEPING the slots, and reaches tokens that carry no device id at all), DELETE /admin/students/devices/revoke, PUT /admin/students/device-limit. The platform default and an on/off switch live in `site_settings` as `max_devices_per_student` and `student_device_limit_enabled`. STUDENT: GET /student/devices, read-only - a student cannot free their own slot, or the limit would be self-service and pointless.

ENFORCEMENT SHIPS OFF, ON PURPOSE. Migration 071 seeds `student_device_limit_enabled` to 0, and the backend reads a missing setting row as off too - so deploying the API before the migration, or without it, cannot lock anyone out. Devices are recorded from the first request while no login is refused, which means the API and the clients can be released in any order. An admin switches enforcement on from Settings once the updated student client is live; by then the device table already shows who is signed in from where, so it is not a leap in the dark. Setting it back to 0 takes effect on the next request and is the escape hatch.

13) OFFLINE PAYMENTS (migration 075, `offline_payment_requests` + `payment_accounts` + the `manage_payments` permission). There is no payment gateway on this platform and none is planned. What actually happened was that a student transferred the money and then tried to reach a human on WhatsApp with a screenshot - nothing recorded who had paid, for what, or whether anyone had looked at it. This gives that flow a queue.

THE RULE THE WHOLE FEATURE RESTS ON: filing a request grants nothing. A request is `pending` until a reviewer approves it, and the amount the student types is never treated as proof - it is stored beside `original_amount` and `discount_amount` so a person compares all three. Recomputing the expected figure at review time was rejected: it would silently follow a later price change and make an old receipt look wrong.

STUDENT: GET /student/payment-accounts (where to send it, no auth), POST /student/offline-payments/quote (what it costs, spends no discount code), POST /student/offline-payments (file it, receipt REQUIRED), GET /student/offline-payments (my requests and why one was rejected), DELETE /student/offline-payments (withdraw a pending one).

ADMIN: GET /admin/offline-payments, POST /admin/offline-payments/review, and full CRUD on /admin/payment-accounts. All behind `manage_payments`, granted to nobody by the migration.

TEACHER: GET /teacher/offline-payments and POST /teacher/offline-payments/review, scoped to the teacher's own courses by the same ownership test the teacher discount codes use. Books are excluded because they already have a teacher review flow of their own.

CONCURRENCY: the approve and reject statements re-check `status = 'pending'` inside the UPDATE. Two reviewers with the same queue open is not hypothetical, and without that exactly that pair of clicks would grant one student two subscriptions to one course.

DISCOUNT CODES: quoting previews one, approving spends one. A request that is never approved costs the student nothing.

CLIENT ACTION: a client that only knows about admin-granted subscriptions will not show a student that they have a payment under review, or why one was refused.

12) APPLICATION SETTINGS ARE REAL NOW (migration 074, `login_attempts` + the `manage_settings` permission). `site_settings` already held `registration_enabled` and `max_login_attempts`. NEITHER of them was read by a single line of PHP, and no dashboard could edit any of them - they were rows that looked like controls and did nothing. They work now, and the admin dashboard has an Application Settings screen for them.

REGISTRATION: POST /user/student/auth/register and /user/parent/auth/register return `error_code: registration_disabled` while the switch is off.

LOGIN LIMIT: counted per (email + IP + role) in the new `login_attempts` table. Per-email counting would have turned the feature into a weapon - anyone knowing the admin's address could lock the admin out of their own platform. `locked_until` is stored in UTC and expires on its own, so no misconfiguration can lock anyone out permanently. Ships OFF even though `max_login_attempts` has held the value 5 for months, because that number was never enforced and switching it on with the migration would have started locking real people out on the strength of a number nobody chose.

EVERY MESSAGE IS BILINGUAL. The stored refusal text is a `_ar` / `_en` pair and both sides are required; the messages built in code - the lockout notice with its minute count, the validation errors, the clear-lockouts confirmation - are chosen by the same `get_request_lang()` the rest of the API uses, so they follow Accept-Language like everything else. A half-filled pair falls back to the other language rather than to an empty string, because a message in the wrong language is still better than no message. CLIENT ACTION: none - branch on `error_code`, never on the text, and render `message` as it arrives.

FIXED HERE: GET /app-config replaces reading the support number off /site-settings, which never worked - see that endpoint for the detail.

NOTHING IN THIS MIGRATION TURNS ANYTHING ON. Every switch is seeded to its inert value and every existing value is left alone, so a real support number is never overwritten by a placeholder.

11) EXAM VISIBILITY AND SORTING. `show_to_students` is now exposed as an explicit alias of `is_active` on an exam, so the show/hide semantics do not have to be inferred from a generic field name. Teacher/admin exam listings take an explicit `sort` (`newest` default, `oldest`; aliases `sort_by`, `order`), and the student-facing exam list filters on `is_active` = 1.

=== WHAT IS NEW IN update-3 ===
update-3 documents Section 10 of the product spec - the Attendance / Delay / Salaries / Deductions system - plus every behavioral change made after update-2. Search this file for the string 'update-3' to find every affected operation.

update-3 introduces 21 brand-new endpoints (teacher wallet + attendance exceptions, student check-in + attendance exceptions, admin HR policy settings, pay rates, exception review, teacher wallets ledger, and deduction appeals), and changes the behavior of several existing ones. It also ships 3 DB migrations (060, 061, 062).

--- GLOBAL BEHAVIOR CHANGES (update-3, apply to EVERY endpoint, not just new ones) ---

1) ACCOUNT DEACTIVATION IS NOW ENFORCED ON EVERY REQUEST. All four auth middlewares (admin/teacher/student/parent) now re-read the caller's own `is_active` column from the DB on each authenticated request. If the row is missing or `is_active = 0`, the request is rejected with HTTP 401 and message `account_inactive` ('الحساب غير مفعل، يرجى التواصل مع الدعم الفني'). Previously a token issued before deactivation kept working until it expired. CLIENT ACTION: treat a 401 carrying that message as a hard logout, not as a 'refresh the token' signal.

2) TOKEN REFRESH IS ALSO GATED. POST /{role}/auth/refresh-token now performs the same `is_active` check before minting new tokens and returns HTTP 403 + `account_inactive` for a deactivated account, so a deactivated user cannot silently renew a session.

3) IMPORTANT DISTINCTION - `is_active` vs `is_attendance_suspended` (teachers only). `teachers.is_active` is the ADMIN's manual enable/disable switch and is the ONLY thing that blocks login/API access (see 1 and 2 above). The NEW column `teachers.is_attendance_suspended` (migration 061) is set automatically by the attendance policy when a teacher exceeds the allowed number of unauthorized absences. It NEVER blocks login and NEVER blocks any API call - it is a pure UI signal telling the teacher app to restrict the teacher to the support chat until an admin lifts it via POST /admin/teacher-wallets/lift-suspension. Do not conflate the two.

4) SERVER CLOCK / TIMEZONE FIX. The default request timezone changed from UTC to Africa/Cairo, and Egypt's reintroduced daylight saving time (forward on the last Friday of April, back on the last Thursday of October) is now computed explicitly instead of trusting the server's stale tzdata. Every time-sensitive value in the API (session start/end matching, check-in lateness, `created_at`, cron no-show detection) is now consistently Cairo local time, UTC+2 in winter and UTC+3 in summer. The `?_timezone=` query parameter still overrides it per request.

5) PAGINATION SCHEMA CORRECTION. The `PaginatedResponse` component in earlier revisions of this file described a `meta {page, limit, total}` envelope that the backend never actually returned. It now documents the real envelope: `pagination {current_page, per_page, total_records, total_pages, has_next_page, has_prev_page}`, plus the optional `statistics` object. No server code changed - the spec was wrong, not the API.

--- HOW THE ATTENDANCE / SALARY SYSTEM FITS TOGETHER (read this before the endpoints) ---

* One global, admin-editable policy row drives everything: GET/PUT /admin/hr-settings (table `hr_policy_settings`, always id = 1). It holds the monthly absence/reschedule limits and the grace period for BOTH roles, the teacher fine amounts, and the default pay model + rate. Changes apply only to sessions evaluated from that moment on - nothing is recalculated retroactively.

* Teacher pay: default comes from the policy row; a per-teacher override can be set with POST /admin/teachers/pay-rate and removed with DELETE /admin/teachers/pay-rate. Three models: `hourly` (rate x minutes/60), `per_session` (flat rate), `per_minute` (rate x minutes).

* Teacher check-in = the EXISTING POST /teacher/sessions/start. Teacher check-out = the EXISTING POST /teacher/sessions/end. There is no separate teacher check-in endpoint. Starting records attendance and may fine lateness; ending computes the session's earning and credits the wallet.

* Student check-in = the NEW POST /student/attendance/check-in, which the app should call right before opening the meeting link.

* Never showing up at all is detected by a cron script (cron/attendance_auto_process.php, runs every minute) at the session's scheduled END time - not at start+grace. Anyone who checks in at any point before the end is 'late'; only a total no-show is 'absent'.

* Excused vs unexcused: an approved absence_permission / late_notice request (POST /teacher|/student/attendance/exceptions, reviewed by admin at PUT /admin/attendance/exceptions) marks that occurrence `is_excused = 1`, which exempts it from fines AND from the monthly unauthorized-absence counter.

* Consequences of crossing the unauthorized-absence limit: a TEACHER gets `is_attendance_suspended = 1` (UI restriction only, see 3 above); a STUDENT gets their subscription frozen (`student_subscriptions.is_active = 0`), which every student-facing endpoint now surfaces as `is_frozen` + `freeze_reason` rather than as a plain 'inactive'/'not subscribed' state.

* Money is an append-only ledger (`teacher_wallet_transactions`) with a cached balance on `teachers.wallet_balance`. Positive amount = credit (earning/refund/positive adjustment), negative = debit (fine/negative adjustment). A teacher may appeal ONLY `fine` rows, once each, via POST /teacher/wallet/appeals; an approved appeal writes a compensating `refund` row.

StudentAuth.description: Student role JWT (some endpoints accept this OPTIONALLY, falling back to ?student_id=)

AnyAuth.description: Any ONE of admin/teacher/student/parent JWTs, tried in that order

PaginatedResponse.description: update-3 (CORRECTION): the real pagination envelope returned by the backend. Earlier revisions of this file wrongly documented a `meta {page, limit, total}` object that no endpoint has ever returned.

statistics.description: Only present on endpoints that compute aggregate counters; omitted otherwise.

HrPolicySettings.description: update-3 (NEW): the single global HR/attendance policy row (`hr_policy_settings`, always id = 1). Every limit, fine and default pay value in the system is read fresh from here at the moment a decision is made, so edits never apply retroactively.

id.description: Always 1 - this table holds exactly one row by design (enforced by a CHECK constraint).

teacher_max_absence_with_permission_per_.description: How many EXCUSED absences a teacher may take per calendar month. Informational/reporting limit - excused absences are already exempt from fines and from the suspension counter.

teacher_max_absence_without_permission.description: Unexcused absences per calendar month before the teacher is auto-flagged `is_attendance_suspended = 1`. Counted from the 1st of the current month.

teacher_max_reschedule_per_month.description: Reschedule requests a teacher may submit per calendar month; the (N+1)th POST /teacher/sessions/reschedule-request is rejected.

teacher_grace_minutes.description: Minutes after the scheduled start within which a teacher check-in still counts as `present`. Beyond it the occurrence becomes `late` and (if not excused) is fined per minute.

teacher_late_fine_per_minute.description: Charged as minutes_late x this value when a teacher checks in late without an approved late_notice. Set to 0 to disable late fines entirely.

teacher_absence_fine_amount.description: Flat fine applied by the cron for a full unexcused no-show. Set to 0 to disable absence fines entirely.

student_max_absence_with_permission_per_.description: Student mirror of the teacher field. Students are never fined - only counted.

student_max_absence_without_permission.description: Unexcused absences per calendar month before the student's subscription is auto-frozen (`student_subscriptions.is_active = 0`).

student_max_reschedule_per_month.description: Reschedule requests a student may submit per calendar month; the (N+1)th POST /student/sessions/reschedule-request is rejected.

student_grace_minutes.description: Minutes after the scheduled start within which a student check-in still counts as `present`.

default_pay_model.description: Used for any teacher with no row in `teacher_pay_rates`.

default_pay_rate.description: The amount that goes with default_pay_model.

TeacherPayRate.description: update-3 (NEW): the effective pay rate for one teacher. This object ALWAYS resolves to something - if the teacher has no personal override row, the values fall back to the global defaults from HrPolicySettings, so the client never has to merge them itself.

TeacherWalletTransaction.description: update-3 (NEW): one immutable row of the teacher wallet ledger (`teacher_wallet_transactions`). Rows are never edited or deleted - a reversal is a new compensating row - so the ledger is a complete audit trail and the sum of `amount` always equals `teachers.wallet_balance`.

type.description: `earning` = pay credited at session check-out. `fine` = automatic deduction (lateness or unexcused absence). `refund` = money returned after an approved appeal. `admin_adjustment` = manual admin correction, either direction.

amount.description: SIGNED. Positive = credit (earning / refund / positive adjustment). Negative = debit (fine / negative adjustment). Display the absolute value with a +/- indicator derived from this sign, do not assume fines are positive.

reference_id.description: class_sessions.id for `session`, teacher_deduction_appeals.id for `appeal`, null for `manual`.

note.description: Human-readable Arabic reason, e.g. 'خصم تأخير 12 دقيقة' or 'أجر حصة'. For admin_adjustment this is the mandatory note the admin typed.

created_by_id.description: The admin id when created_by_type = 'admin'; null when the system wrote the row.

can_appeal.description: update-3: convenience flag present ONLY on the teacher-facing GET /teacher/wallet/transactions. True exactly when type = 'fine'. Use it to decide whether to render the 'Appeal' button; the server still re-validates, and also rejects a second appeal on the same transaction.

AttendanceExceptionRequest.description: update-3 (NEW): one absence-with-permission or late-notice request (`attendance_exception_requests`). The exact same object shape is returned to the teacher, the student and the admin - only the `requester` sub-object differs by role.

occurrence_date.description: The specific calendar date this request covers. class_sessions rows are WEEKLY RECURRING templates (one row per weekday/time), so a request is always pinned to one occurrence, never to the whole series.

request_type.description: `absence_permission` = 'I will miss this occurrence entirely'. `late_notice` = 'I will attend but arrive late'.

expected_minutes_late.description: Required and > 0 for late_notice; null for absence_permission.

session.description: The fully resolved class session object (same shape used across the sessions endpoints), embedded so no second call is needed to render the row.

requester.description: The person who filed it. For a student: {id, name, email, image}. For a teacher the same plus {is_active, is_attendance_suspended} - so the admin review screen can see at a glance whether this teacher is already attendance-suspended.

TeacherDeductionAppeal.description: update-3 (NEW): a teacher's objection to one `fine` wallet transaction (`teacher_deduction_appeals`). At most one appeal per transaction, ever.

teacher.description: {id, name, email, image} of the appealing teacher.

TeacherWalletRow.description: update-3 (NEW): one teacher as shown on the admin 'teacher wallets' screen - identity, both status flags, cached balance and effective pay rate in a single row, so that screen needs no per-teacher follow-up calls.

is_active.description: The ADMIN's manual enable/disable switch. 0 here means the teacher genuinely cannot log in.

is_attendance_suspended.description: update-3 (NEW column, migration 061): set automatically by the attendance policy. Does NOT block login - render it as a separate 'attendance-suspended' badge, never as 'Inactive'. Clear it with POST /admin/teacher-wallets/lift-suspension.

wallet_balance.description: Cached sum of every ledger row for this teacher.

FrozenStateFlags.description: update-3 (NEW, added to several student-facing objects): tells 'frozen because of the attendance policy' apart from 'expired' and from 'never subscribed'. A subscription's is_active is ONLY ever set to 0 by the attendance auto-freeze, so is_frozen is unambiguous. Render it as 'مجمد' (Frozen), NOT as 'غير فعال' (Inactive), and offer a contact-support action.

is_frozen.description: true when the subscription/course access exists but is currently frozen for excessive unauthorized absence (is_active = 0 AND not expired).

freeze_reason.description: Localized, ready-to-display explanation when is_frozen is true; null otherwise. Arabic: 'تم تجميد اشتراكك تلقائيًا لتجاوزك الحد المسموح به من الغياب بدون إذن...'.

ExamSummary.description: One exam from `course_exams`. EVERY exam always carries a non-null `course_id` (the admin/teacher UI requires picking a course to create any exam) - `unit_id` is what distinguishes a unit-scoped exam from a whole-course exam, it is null for the latter.

course_id.description: Always set in practice - see the type description.

unit_id.description: null = whole-course exam. Set = this exam belongs to one specific unit inside course_id.

is_active.description: update-4 (CLARIFIED): this IS the 'show exam to students' toggle - GET /student/exams filters on is_active = 1, so an admin/teacher setting this to 0 (via PUT /admin/exams or PUT /teacher/exams) immediately hides the exam from every student, with no other side effect. See also the explicit alias `show_to_students` below.

unit.description: update-3 (NEW): lightweight {id, name}, present only when unit_id is set. Lets the client label/group unit exams without a second lookup per row.

course.description: update-3 (NEW): full course details (same shape as elsewhere in the API), present whenever course_id is set - i.e. on every exam in practice.

subject.description: update-3 (NEW): full subject details, present only when subject_id is set (rare - most exams are scoped to a course or a unit, not a bare subject).

my_attempt.description: The calling student's own attempt at this exam, if any: {id, status, total_score, max_score}. null if they have never started it.

show_to_students.description: update-4 (NEW): explicit alias of `is_active` for this exam, added so the show/hide-to-students semantics don't have to be inferred from a generically-named `is_active` field. Always equal to `is_active`.

TeacherHomeResponse.description: update-4 (REWRITE): the teacher dashboard home screen. Every field is computed live from the DB - the previous version of this endpoint returned hardcoded demo data (fake KPI numbers, a fixed 7-month chart, 3 made-up 'recent activity' rows) whenever the real query came back empty; none of that placeholder behavior remains.

teacher.description: Core profile snapshot for the header. NOTE: this is a lighter object than GET /teacher/auth/profile (no city/experience/qualifications/metrics) - fetch that endpoint separately for the full profile screen.

rating.description: Real average from `teachers.rating`, which is recomputed on every new approved student rating - not a placeholder.

reviews_count.description: COUNT of approved rows in `teacher_ratings` for this teacher.

is_attendance_suspended.description: Section 10 automatic attendance restriction - separate from is_active, never blocks login (see the account-suspension notes on other endpoints).

subjects.description: Every subject this teacher is assigned to, from get_teacher_subjects_details().

kpis.description: Single-number summary cards for the top of the dashboard - every value also appears in more detail further down in the response (wallet, today, pending_actions).

total_students.description: Distinct students subscribed to this teacher directly, or to any course/subject they teach.

total_courses.description: Courses/packages this teacher owns or is linked to (course_teachers), active only.

total_active_sessions.description: Count of this teacher's active weekly class_sessions rows (their whole recurring schedule, not just today).

pending_actions_count.description: Sum of every counter in `pending_actions` - use this for a single badge/notification-dot.

wallet.description: Section 10 (attendance/salary system) snapshot - same numbers as GET /teacher/wallet, embedded here to save the home screen a second call.

sessions.description: Full session detail objects for every one of the teacher's active class_sessions scheduled today - same shape and same status/is_available_now/meeting_link logic as GET /teacher/sessions, so a client already rendering that screen can reuse its card component here unchanged.

pending_actions.description: Everything currently waiting on this teacher, broken out so the UI can deep-link each count to its own screen.

pending_homework_grading_count.description: homework_submissions with status='submitted' for homework this teacher created.

pending_exam_grading_count.description: exam_attempts with status='submitted' (i.e. containing at least one written question awaiting manual grading) for exams this teacher owns - same ownership rule as teacher_owns_exam().

incoming_reschedule_requests_count.description: Pending session_reschedule_requests filed BY a student, addressed to this teacher (see PUT /teacher/sessions/reschedule-requests/review).

my_attendance_exception_requests_pending.description: This teacher's OWN absence/late-notice requests still awaiting admin review (Section 10).

put.description:
CASE (decision=rejected): only id/decision/admin_note matter, everything else below is ignored.
CASE (decision=approved, 3 sub-scenarios):
1) Default (no keep_original_schedule, no new_day/time overrides) -> applies the teacher's own originally-requested new_day/new_start_time/new_end_time as-is.
2) new_day/new_start_time/new_end_time sent -> OVERRIDES the teacher's requested time with the admin's own choice instead.
3) keep_original_schedule=true -> ignores any new day/time entirely, keeps the session at its CURRENT day/time, and instead REASSIGNS it to new_teacher_id (which becomes REQUIRED in this case and is validated against that teacher's course/subject+grade assignment).

update-3 (CHANGED): the decision logic is unchanged, but the requesting TEACHER is now notified of the outcome (previously no notification was sent at all on this route, so teachers never learned their request had been answered). The notification body names the teacher explicitly, because the same record also surfaces in the admin's global notification log where an unnamed 'your request' carries no information.

post.description: update-3 (CHANGED - Section 10): ending a session is now ALSO the teacher's check-out and the moment their pay is calculated. On the FIRST end-call for that date the server: (1) looks up the teacher_session_attendance row for this occurrence - if there is none, or its status is 'absent', nothing is paid (you cannot earn for a session you never started); (2) computes duration = check_out_time minus check_in_time in minutes, floored at 1 - this is ACTUAL elapsed time, not the scheduled length; (3) applies the teacher's effective pay model (hourly = rate x minutes/60, per_session = flat rate, per_minute = rate x minutes); (4) writes an `earning` ledger row for that amount and increases teachers.wallet_balance. IDEMPOTENT: a row that already has a check_out_time is never paid a second time, so retried/duplicate end-calls are safe. Note that lateness fines are charged at START, not here.

post.summary: update-4 (CHANGED): Student login - now device-limited
post.description:
update-1: response now also includes is_subscribed on the student object (same computation as the one already returned by the profile endpoint: true if the student has at least one accessible course via get_student_accessible_entities()).

=== update-4 (BREAKING FOR CLIENTS): DEVICE LIMIT ===

An account may only be signed in from a limited number of devices - one by default. One set of credentials shared around a class was the cheapest way to give a paid course away, and nothing noticed it before.

CLIENT ACTION, REQUIRED: send a `device_id` with every login (body field, or the `X-Device-Id` header). It must be an id the client generates ONCE and keeps - a random uuid in localStorage is enough. Do NOT generate a fresh one per login: the server counts devices, so a new id every time burns through the student's slots immediately. Optional `device_name` and `platform` are what an admin sees in the devices list, so send something human.

While the limit is enabled, a login with NO device id is REFUSED with `error_code: device_id_required`. Letting an unidentified client through would make the whole limit decorative - anyone could drop the field for unlimited sessions.

TWO NEW REFUSALS, both HTTP 200 with `status: "error"` and an `error_code` to branch on:
- `device_id_required` - the client sent no device id.
- `device_limit_reached` - the account is already at its ceiling. The response also carries `max_devices` and `active_devices`. This is NOT a wrong-password error and must not be shown as one: the message tells the student to contact support, because only an admin can free a slot (POST /admin/students/devices/reset).

A device that has signed in before reuses its own slot, so signing in again from the same browser is always allowed.

ON EVERY LATER REQUEST: the access token now carries the device id, and the student auth middleware re-checks that the device is still authorised. A revoked device gets HTTP 401 with `error_code: device_revoked` - treat that as a hard logout, not as a refresh-the-token signal. POST /auth/refresh is gated the same way and answers 403 with the same code, so a revoked device cannot mint itself fresh tokens.

Tokens issued BEFORE this change carry no device id and are left alone, so turning the limit on does not sign out everyone already logged in.

A parent viewing their child (POST /parent/auth/login-as-student) mints a student token with no device id: it does not consume one of the child's slots and is never blocked by the child's limit.

TURNING IT OFF: set `site_settings.student_device_limit_enabled` to `0`. Devices are still recorded, but nothing is refused - use this if a client that cannot be updated yet has to keep working.

update-4 (CHANGED): subject to the login limit when `login_lockout_enabled` is on (migration 074). After `max_login_attempts` failures the response is `error_code: login_locked` with `retry_after_minutes`, and the CORRECT password is refused too until the lock expires. Counted per (email + IP + role), so an attacker can only ever lock out their own address - not the account holder's. The lock expires on its own; an admin can release every lock with POST /admin/login-attempts/clear. Ships OFF.

device_id.description: update-4: REQUIRED while the device limit is enabled. An id the client generates once and KEEPS (a uuid in localStorage). A fresh id per login burns through the student's device slots. May also be sent as the `X-Device-Id` header.

post.description:
update-1: Lets admin subscribe a plain student to a specific course, a whole subject (grants every course under it, scoped to the student's own academic_year_id), or a whole teacher (grants everything that teacher teaches, also scoped to the student's own academic_year_id) — all three without generating or using any subscription code. subscription_type is derived automatically from which *_ids array is non-empty (course_ids only -> 'course', subject_ids only -> 'subject', teacher_ids only -> 'teacher', a mix -> 'custom'). update-4 (BEHAVIOUR CHANGE): when neither `end_date` nor `duration_days` is sent and the granted courses include a package, the subscription's `end_date` becomes start + the longest selected package's `courses.duration_months`. Package grants used to be stored with `end_date` NULL, i.e. access that never expired.

update-4: the response now also carries a `discount` object when `discount_code` was sent - either the applied amounts or the reason the code was refused.

discount_code.description:
update-4 (NEW): applies a discount code to this grant. THIS is where a code is spent - the redemption is recorded against the new subscription and the code's `used_count` goes up. An invalid code does NOT cancel the grant: the access was requested deliberately, so the subscription is still created and the failure is reported in the response's `discount` object.

update-4 (BEHAVIOUR CHANGE): OMITTING this field no longer means 'no discount'. When it is empty and `course_ids` was sent, the server looks up the student's own pending claims (POST /student/discount-codes/apply) for those courses and honours the first still-valid one, so a code the student picked themselves is not lost just because the admin did not retype it. The response's `discount` object carries `from_student_claim: true` when that happened. To grant with NO discount at all for a student who is holding a code, the claim has to be dropped first - there is no 'ignore the claim' flag.

update-4 (VALIDATION CHANGE): a discount is now REFUSED when the grant has no courses - i.e. on a subject-wide or teacher-wide grant. Only a course or a package carries a price, so there was nothing to reduce; the old behaviour still recorded a redemption of 0.00, which spent one of the code's uses and, with `once_per_student`, burnt that code for that student permanently in exchange for no discount. The subscription is still created; the refusal is reported in `discount.message`.

post.summary: update-3 (NEW): Teacher files an absence-with-permission or late-notice request for one session occurrence
post.description:
update-3 (NEW, Section 10). The teacher's way to avoid being fined for a class they already know they will miss or be late to. The request always goes to the ADMIN for review (PUT /admin/attendance/exceptions) - never to another teacher.

WHY IT MATTERS: once approved, that occurrence is marked `is_excused = 1`, which (a) suppresses the automatic fine and (b) keeps it out of the monthly unauthorized-absence counter that would otherwise eventually set `is_attendance_suspended = 1`. A rejected or never-filed request means the normal automatic consequences apply.

VALIDATION, in the order the server checks it:
1. session_id > 0 and a parseable occurrence_date, else `session_id_and_date_required`.
2. request_type must be exactly 'absence_permission' or 'late_notice', else `request_type_required`.
3. reason must be non-empty, else `reason_required`.
4. for 'late_notice', expected_minutes_late must be present and > 0, else `expected_minutes_late_required`.
5. the session must exist AND belong to this teacher, else `session_not_found_or_not_owned`.
6. there must be no OTHER still-pending request from this same teacher for this same (session_id, occurrence_date), else `request_already_pending`. Note this only blocks duplicates while one is pending - after a rejection the teacher may file again.

SIDE EFFECT: all admins get a push/in-app notification naming the teacher and the request type.

occurrence_date.description: The single date this applies to, e.g. '2026-09-20'. Alias `date` is also accepted. Sessions are weekly templates, so this is what pins the request to one specific class.

request_type.description: absence_permission = will miss it entirely. late_notice = will attend but arrive late.

expected_minutes_late.description: REQUIRED and must be > 0 when request_type = 'late_notice'. Ignored for absence_permission.

update-3 (NEW, Section 10). The student-side counterpart of the teacher's POST /teacher/sessions/start. Call it the moment the student taps 'Join', then open `meeting_link` regardless of the outcome - treat it as best-effort telemetry, never as a gate on the UI.

WHAT IT DOES: writes today's row in `session_attendance` for this (session, student). Lateness = now minus the session's scheduled start_time, in minutes, floored at 0. Status is `present` while that stays within `student_grace_minutes` from the policy, and `late` beyond it. If the student already has an APPROVED late_notice for this exact occurrence, the row is additionally marked `is_excused = 1`, which keeps it out of the monthly unauthorized-absence counter. Students are never fined money for lateness.

IDEMPOTENT: repeated calls update status/lateness but never overwrite the original `check_in_time` and never re-fire the notification. Only the FIRST check-in of the day notifies the teacher ('a student has already joined, please do not be late').

ACCESS CHECK: the student must currently have access to the session's course, subject or teacher. A student whose subscription is FROZEN fails this check with `not_subscribed_to_session` - which is intended: a frozen student cannot join classes, they can only see them.

NOT calling this endpoint is exactly how a no-show is detected: at the session's scheduled END time the cron marks every subscribed student with no row as absent.

put.description:
update-3 (NEW, Section 10). PARTIAL BY DESIGN: send only the fields you want to change; anything omitted keeps its current value. Sending an empty/unknown-only body is an error (`no_fields_to_update`) rather than a silent no-op.

SANITISATION: all integer fields are clamped to >= 0, all decimal fields to >= 0, and `default_pay_model` is only accepted from the enum - an invalid value is silently ignored rather than saved. The response re-reads the row from the DB, so what you get back is exactly what is now stored.

TIMING SEMANTICS (important, and matches the product spec): changes are NEVER retroactive. Fines already charged, absences already counted and earnings already credited stay as they were; the new numbers only affect sessions and requests evaluated from this moment on, because every consumer reads this row fresh at decision time.

post.description:
update-3 (NEW, Section 10). Pins one teacher to their own pay model/rate, overriding `default_pay_model` / `default_pay_rate` from the policy row. UPSERT: calling it again for the same teacher replaces the existing override rather than erroring or creating a duplicate.

The three models and how the earning is computed at check-out:
- `hourly`      -> rate_amount x (actual minutes / 60), rounded to 2 decimals. Pays for real time spent.
- `per_session` -> flat rate_amount regardless of duration.
- `per_minute`  -> rate_amount x actual minutes.
'Actual minutes' means check_out_time minus check_in_time (floored at 1 minute), NOT the scheduled length - a session that runs long pays more on the time-based models.

Takes effect on the teacher's NEXT check-out; already-credited earnings are untouched.

Validation: teacher_id must reference a real teacher (`teacher_not_found`), pay_model must be in the enum (`pay_model_required`), rate_amount must be present and >= 0 (`rate_amount_required`).

- an approved `absence_permission` makes the no-show cron record that occurrence as absent-but-EXCUSED, with NO fine for a teacher and NO increment of the monthly unauthorized-absence counter for either role;
- an approved `late_notice` makes the check-in flow mark the late arrival as excused, so a late teacher is not fined per minute.
This is why approving retroactively, after the cron has already run for that occurrence, will not undo a fine - use POST /admin/teacher-wallets/adjust or the appeal flow for that.

Only a request still in `pending` can be decided; anything else returns `request_not_found_or_reviewed`, which also makes the endpoint safe against double-submits.

post.summary: update-3 (NEW): Manually credit or debit a teacher's wallet
post.description:
update-3 (NEW, Section 10). The escape hatch for anything the automatic rules cannot express: a bonus, a correction, a fine the admin wants to apply by hand, or refunding something the appeal flow does not cover.

`amount` is SIGNED - send a positive number to credit the teacher and a NEGATIVE number to debit them. Zero is rejected (`amount_required`).

`note` is MANDATORY (`note_required`), because the resulting ledger row is permanent and the teacher will see this text as the explanation for the movement. The row is written with `type = 'admin_adjustment'`, `reference_type = 'manual'` and `created_by_type = 'admin'` with the acting admin's id, so manual money is always distinguishable from automatic money in the audit trail.

post.summary: update-3 (CHANGED): Start a live session - now also the teacher's attendance check-in, and blocked earlier than 5 minutes before the start time
post.description:
update-3: this pre-existing endpoint gained TWO behaviors. It is documented here for the first time because both are breaking-ish for clients.

1) NEW HARD TIME GATE. The call is REJECTED with `session_start_too_early` if it arrives more than 5 minutes before the session's scheduled `start_time`. In other words the allowed window opens at start_time minus 5 minutes and never closes (starting late is permitted - and is exactly what produces a 'late' record). The 5 minutes is a fixed constant, NOT the configurable `teacher_grace_minutes` (which governs the opposite side: how late is still 'present').
CLIENT ACTION: the teacher app must surface this message as an alert and keep the Start button disabled until the window opens. And because this error is returned with HTTP 200 and `status: 'error'` in the body, any client that shows a success toast purely on a 2xx will show the error text inside a green toast - branch on the body's `status`.

2) IT IS NOW THE TEACHER'S CHECK-IN. On the FIRST successful call for a given date the server records `teacher_session_attendance` for that occurrence: lateness = now minus start_time in minutes (floored at 0); status = `present` while within `teacher_grace_minutes`, `late` beyond it. If the teacher is `late`, has NO approved late_notice for that occurrence, and `teacher_late_fine_per_minute` > 0, a `fine` ledger row of minutes_late x rate is written immediately and the teacher is notified of the deduction. The subscribed students are also notified that the teacher has joined.
IDEMPOTENT: repeat calls the same day do not re-record, re-fine or re-notify.

There is intentionally no separate teacher check-in endpoint - this is it.

post.description:
update-3: two changes to this pre-existing endpoint.

1) MONTHLY CAP. Before inserting, the server counts this teacher's reschedule requests created since the 1st of the current month. If that count already reaches `teacher_max_reschedule_per_month` from the HR policy, the request is refused with `max_reschedule_requests_reached` ('تم الوصول للحد الأقصى من طلبات التأجيل المسموح بها هذا الشهر'). Note the counter is on requests SUBMITTED, not requests approved - a rejected request still consumes one slot.

2) BUGFIX - `new_start_time` / `new_end_time` are truly optional now. The code always treated them as optional (a reschedule may move only the DAY and keep the same time), but the DB columns were NOT NULL, so omitting them crashed with a raw SQL error "Column 'new_start_time' cannot be null". Migration 062 makes both columns nullable. Omitting them now correctly means 'keep the original time'.

3) NOTIFICATION. All admins are now notified on creation, and the message NAMES the teacher (previously such messages were anonymous, which made the admin's notification log unreadable).

get.description:
update-3: every subscription object returned anywhere in the API (student, admin list, admin details - all three copies of the resolver were updated) now carries two new fields:
- `is_frozen` (boolean): true when `is_active = 0` AND the subscription has NOT merely expired.
- `freeze_reason` (string|null): a ready-to-display localized explanation when frozen, null otherwise.

This is unambiguous because `student_subscriptions.is_active` is set to 0 by exactly ONE code path in the entire backend - the attendance auto-freeze. Expiry is tracked separately via `end_date`, and admins do not toggle this column by hand.

CLIENT ACTION: where the UI used to print 'غير فعال' (Inactive) for is_active = 0, print 'مجمد' (Frozen) instead when is_frozen is true, show `freeze_reason`, and offer a contact-support action. 'Inactive' is now reserved for genuinely expired/ended subscriptions.

Now the list is the UNION of (a) courses the student can currently access and (b) courses whose only grant is a frozen subscription. Every returned course object gains:
- `is_frozen` (boolean): true ONLY for courses in group (b) - i.e. it is false for a course the student can still reach through some other active grant, even if a different frozen subscription also covered it.
- `freeze_reason` (string|null).

get.summary: update-3: List exams available to the student - defaults to WHOLE-COURSE exams only when filtering by course_id; unit exams are opt-in
get.description:
Every exam in the system always has a non-null `course_id` (the creation UI requires picking a course first, whether the exam is a whole-course exam or a unit exam - `unit_id` is only set for the latter, on top of the same course_id). Because of that, this endpoint treats `course_id` requests differently depending on `include_unit_exams` - READ THIS BEFORE CALLING IT WITH course_id:

1) `course_id` ALONE (default, `include_unit_exams` unset/`0`/`false`) -> returns ONLY whole-course exams for that course (`unit_id IS NULL`). Unit exams belonging to that course are DELIBERATELY excluded - this is the default precisely so a course-details screen doesn't unexpectedly show unit exams mixed in with the course's own exam.
2) `course_id` + `unit_id` -> returns exams for that ONE specific unit only (existing, unchanged behavior) - `include_unit_exams` is ignored in this case.
3) `course_id` + `include_unit_exams=1` (alias: `with_unit_exams=1`) -> returns the COMBINED list: the whole-course exam(s) AND every unit exam under that course, mixed together in one array. Use this for an aggregated 'all exams in this course' screen/tab - each item still carries its own `unit_id`/`unit` object (null for the whole-course ones) so the client can group or label them.
4) `course_id` + `include_unit_exams=only` -> returns UNIT EXAMS ONLY for that course (`unit_id IS NOT NULL`), EXCLUDING the whole-course exam(s) entirely. Use this for a screen that lists only per-unit exams, with no whole-course exam mixed in.

`unit_id` alone (no course_id) and `subject_id` alone keep their original, unrelated behavior - filtering directly on that column, unaffected by any of the above.

Access control (unrelated to the scoping above): an exam is only returned if the student is subscribed to its subject or its course - a student with no subscriptions at all gets an empty list immediately, before any of the filters run.

update-4 (SORTING): results are now explicitly ordered - previously this endpoint had NO ORDER BY at all, so the order was undefined (effectively storage-engine dependent) and could silently change between calls. The default is now NEWEST FIRST (by `created_at` then `id`, descending). Use the `sort` parameter to reverse it.

update-4 (VISIBILITY): only exams with `is_active` (= `show_to_students`) equal to 1 are ever returned here - an exam an admin or teacher has hidden via PUT /admin/exams or PUT /teacher/exams (`is_active: 0`) disappears from this list immediately and unconditionally, regardless of any other filter in this request.

- unset / `0` / `false` (default): whole-course exams only.
- `1` / `true`: COMBINED - whole-course exam(s) + every unit exam under the course.
- `only` (aliases: `unit_only`, `units_only`): UNIT EXAMS ONLY - excludes the whole-course exam(s) entirely.

get.summary: update-4 (REWRITE): Teacher dashboard home - fully real, wired to every teacher-relevant system
get.description:
Complete rewrite of this endpoint. The previous implementation was demo/placeholder code: every KPI had a hardcoded fallback number (e.g. a fake '24512 students' / '$84254 revenue') that was returned whenever the real query came back empty or zero, a 7-month chart with fixed fake numbers, and 3 hardcoded 'recent activity' rows naming students who don't exist in this database. NONE of that remains - every field below is a live, real query against this teacher's own data, and a genuinely empty result now correctly reads as zero/empty rather than being papered over with a fake number.

This is the single aggregate call for a teacher app's home/dashboard screen, pulling together:
- Profile snapshot + real rating/reviews (`teacher`).
- Top-line KPI cards (`kpis`).
- Section 10 wallet balance and effective pay rate (`wallet`) - same numbers as GET /teacher/wallet.
- Today's full schedule with live status per session (`today`) - same session objects as GET /teacher/sessions.
- Every action currently awaiting this teacher, broken out per source, so the UI can deep-link each one (`pending_actions`): ungraded homework submissions, ungraded exam attempts, incoming student reschedule requests, this teacher's own pending Section 10 exception requests and deduction appeals, and pending consultation bookings.
- A preview of up to 6 owned courses/packages with real student counts (`my_courses`).
- The next 5 approved+booked consultations (`upcoming_consultations`).
- The 5 most recent notifications (`recent_notifications`).

Both GET /teacher/home and GET /teacher/content/home hit the exact same handler (`teacherHome`) - they are not two different implementations, just two paths that existed already.

- `statistics.courses` - course count, alongside the existing entity counts.
- `sales` - total / today / this month / this year revenue, plus a per-channel breakdown.
- `top_courses` - sales and revenue per course, best seller first.
- `charts.sales_by_month` and `charts.students_by_month` - always exactly 12 entries (January to December), including months with no data, so a chart can be rendered without filling gaps client-side.
- `recent_activity` - newest platform events, each with a `link` to the page that handles it.

post.summary: update-4 (NEW): Sign a student out of every session
post.description:
Ends every session the student has open, everywhere, immediately.

DIFFERENT FROM RESETTING DEVICES, and both are worth having:
- POST /admin/students/devices/reset frees the SLOTS, so a NEW device can sign in.
- this ends every SESSION, so the SAME device simply has to sign in again.

The second is what you want when a phone goes missing: end the sessions without also costing the student the device slot they will want back in an hour. Send `revoke_devices: true` to do both at once.

It also reaches sessions device revocation cannot see. Rather than looking for a device id, it stamps `students.sessions_revoked_at` and every token issued before that moment is refused - so tokens minted before devices existed, or while the limit was switched off, die too.

Both the auth middleware and POST /auth/refresh enforce it, so a signed-out session cannot refresh its way back in. Clients get `error_code: session_revoked` (HTTP 401 on a normal call, 403 on refresh) and should treat it as a hard logout. A login AFTER the cutoff is unaffected.

post.summary: update-4 (NEW): Apply a discount code (student actually USING it)
post.description:
The student using a code rather than previewing it. There is no payment gateway in this platform, so using a code cannot mean paying with it: this PINS the code to the course or package the student wants. The claim is stored as a `pending` row on `discount_code_redemptions`, the code's `used_count` is NOT touched, and the admin's later grant is what turns it into a real discount.

Why this matters to a client: after a successful apply, the student does not have to relay the code to support by hand. POST /admin/subscriptions with NO `discount_code` in the body now looks the student's pending claims up itself and honours the first still-valid one for the granted courses.

Idempotent per student + code + course: pressing the button twice re-reads the same claim and re-prices it instead of stacking rows. Requires a logged-in student - an anonymous visitor has nothing to pin a code to, and gets an error rather than a silent no-op.

Rejected for the same reasons as a check (inactive, not started, expired, fully used, wrong course, already used by this student), and the message explains which.

course_ids.description: Alternative to course_id when several are wanted at once. At least one course is REQUIRED: only a course or package carries a price, so there is nothing for a code to reduce without one.

Everything else - the landing page copy, the stats labels - stays free text. The validator is deliberately not a whitelist, or the website editor would silently stop saving.

post.summary: update-4 (NEW): Approve or reject a payment
post.description:
update-4 (NEW). Body: `id`, `action` ('approve' or 'reject'), `note`.

Approving opens the access, records the subscription it created in `granted_ref_id`, and spends the discount code if the request carried one - the code is consumed HERE and not when the request was filed.

Rejecting REQUIRES a note, because the student is shown it. A rejected request keeps its row and its reason: 'this is the third receipt this month that did not match' is exactly what someone needs later.

The status is re-checked inside the UPDATE, so of two reviewers with the same queue open exactly one wins and the student never ends up with two subscriptions to one course.

Requires `manage_payments`.

post.summary: update-4 (NEW): Add an account
post.description:
update-4 (NEW). BANK TRANSFER ONLY. The local wallets this shipped with (InstaPay, Vodafone Cash and the rest) were dropped: they exist in Egypt and nowhere else, and this platform can be run from outside it. A bank account is the one instrument that travels.

Body: `label_ar`, `label_en`, `account_number` (required), plus optional `bank_name`, `swift_code`, `account_name`, `instructions_ar`, `instructions_en`, `is_active`, `sort_order`. `method` may be omitted; 'bank' is the only accepted value.

`account_number` is required because it IS the feature: an account row without one tells a student to transfer money to nowhere. `swift_code`, when given, must be a valid 8 or 11 character BIC - it is what a bank abroad routes on, and a mistyped one fails at the sending bank with no useful explanation.

The migration seeds one sample account INACTIVE. An active account is shown to students as somewhere to send real money, so placeholder details stay hidden until a person has replaced them and switched it on. Requires `manage_payments`.
